label: D2: arrived at S2 when a1 was chosen (rare a1->S2) or a1 was the previous choice
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the state shown is S2 (in_state==2 covers 99.98% of activations; never on D1/GO or S1). Within S2 it fires on 29% of steps, chiefly when S2 is unexpected given the agent a1 leaning: the rare transition a1->S2 (precision 0.92, F1 0.83 alone; ~84% of mass, and the strongest activations), plus common a2->S2 right after the agent switched away from a1 (prev_action==1). All variables are observed at D2. Equivalent readout: D2 & S2 & policy logit(a1)-logit(a2) > -1 scores F1 0.88 / mass recall 0.96 on dev, so the unit tracks reaching S2 while the agent does not (yet) strongly favor a2. Misses are weak activations on a2->S2 common steps within long a2 runs; false positives are a1->S2 rare steps after repeated rare outcomes. Silent on a2->S2 when the agent firmly prefers a2.

issues: The core claims hold on test. Phase != D2 has recall 0 (it never fires at D1 or GO), and D2 & in_state==2 has recall 0.9999 with precision 0.29, so it does fire on about 29% of S2 steps.
The rare a1->S2 clause is a little weaker on test than reported. Precision is 0.919 (claimed 0.92) but F1 is 0.807 (claimed 0.83) and mass recall 0.807 (claimed about 84%).

The second clause overclaims. On test, D2 & S2 & a2 & prev_action==1 has precision only 0.57 and recall 0.099. Split by the previous reward, the unit fires after an unrewarded a1 (precision 0.91) and is mostly silent after a rewarded a1 (precision 0.15, the model-based switch after rare-rewarded). So 'or when the previous choice was a1' is the wrong condition. Tightening it to prev_action==1 & prev_reward==0 raises test precision from 0.856 to 0.918 and F1 from 0.837 to 0.859.

There is a systematic miss class, not scattered noise. Of the active steps, 10,909 on test (about 18% of activations, 9.8% of the mass) are common a2->S2 steps where a2 was also chosen on the previous trial. The rendered windows usually follow one or more unrewarded trials, so the agent's preference for a2 is weak. The explanation's 'long runs of a2' is only partly right: D2 & S2 & a2 & prev_a2 & prev_reward==0 has precision 0.17, so the misses are not cleanly captured by observed history.

The policy readout explains the unit better than the recorded predicate: D2 & S2 & choice > -1 gives test precision 0.858, recall 0.898, F1 0.878, mass recall 0.964 (choice > -0.5 gives F1 0.878). The explanation itself says this; 'only about 3 F1 points lower' is roughly right (4 points on test), but the policy-based description is the more faithful one.
